_transcription: ENGLISH half only, CBSE Class 10 Mathematics Standard (041), Series C3ABD/1, SET 3. 16 pages: idx 0 bilingual cover, idx 1 Hindi instructions + Hindi Q1-4; English on every even index 2-14, Hindi on every odd index 1-13 (each the Hindi of the page after it); odd-page tops checked on the contact sheet, all open in Hindi; idx 15 is blank (confirmed at full size, no English, no ghost); last English page idx 14. General Instructions (i)-(x) confirm full80: 38 questions, A Q1-18 MCQ + Q19-20 A-R @1, B Q21-25 @2, C Q26-31 @3, D Q32-35 @5, E Q36-38 case studies @4. Instruction (viii) prints 2 internal choices in B, 2 in C, 2 in D and 3 of 2 marks in E: Q22, Q23, Q29, Q30, Q33, Q34, Q36, Q37, Q38, all found on the paper, and the marking-scheme walk shows exactly these nine OR blocks. Main-question alternatives are printed (A)/(B), case-study alternatives (a)/(b); questionNumbers follow the printed labels. Section-A keys read off the marking scheme for 30/1/3 as images and each re-derived: all agree; no void notes anywhere in the scheme. Decimal points are ORDINARY full stops on this paper (Q35). Section E prints no 'Case Study - N' headings, so no _caseStudyLabel. Sibling of 30/1/1: 43 rows are the same questions as 30/1/1 (confirmed on these pages, text reused byte-for-byte from that file), 10 rows are new to this set (Q2, Q7, Q9, Q16, Q24, Q25, Q26, Q27, Q32, Q35). Every _figure note was written from this paper's own pages. The two case-study photographs on idx 14 render mostly black in this scan; both are decorative.

**Assertion (A) :** The tangents drawn at the end points of a diameter of a circle, are parallel.

**Reason (R) :** Diameter of a circle is the longest chord.

questions.subtopic: Median of Grouped Data
questions._figure: DECORATIVE - a photograph of BINGO balls over a number strip (rendered mostly black in this scan); every number is in the passage and table. Page idx 14.
questions.context:
BINGO is game of chance. The host has 75 balls numbered 1 through 75. Each player has a BINGO card with some numbers written on it. The participant cancels the number on the card when called out a number written on the ball selected at random. Whosoever cancels all the numbers on his/her card, says BINGO and wins the game.

The table given below, shows the data of one such game where 48 balls were used before Tara said 'BINGO'.

| Numbers announced | Number of times |
|---|---|
| 0-15 | 8 |
| 15-30 | 9 |
| 30-45 | 10 |
| 45-60 | 12 |
| 60-75 | 9 |

Based on the above information, answer the following :
questions.stem: Write the median class.
